name: Bhutan: Phuentsholing, Thimphu and Paro
one_line: Western Bhutan from the border gate at Phuentsholing to Thimphu, over Dochula to Punakha, and across to Paro

highway.value: Phuentsholing to Thimphu road and the East-West Highway (Lateral Road)

usual_season.value: Late September to late November; open all year

fuel.note: Pumps are those drawn on the open map within the search radius of the road. A pump missing from the map is missing here, so each gap is a worst case.

rules.title: Bhutan: entry permit, not a visa, for Indians
rules.detail: Apply online before travel or at the point of entry, where waits can be long. Land permits are issued at Phuentsholing and three other border immigration offices.
rules.set_by: Department of Immigration, Royal Government of Bhutan

history.change: Covid vaccination no longer required to enter, per the Indian embassy's guidelines.

source.title: Guidelines For Indians visiting Bhutan as Tourists

rules.title: Bhutan: passport or voter card
rules.detail: A passport valid six months or an original voter identity card, plus two photographs. Under-18s use a passport or birth certificate and travel with a legal guardian.
rules.set_by: Department of Immigration, Royal Government of Bhutan

source.title: Guidelines For Indians visiting Bhutan as Tourists

rules.title: Bhutan: 1,200 a night Sustainable Development Fee
rules.detail: Indian visitors pay 1,200 ngultrum or rupees per person per night when applying for the permit. Young children are exempt; older children pay half.
rules.set_by: Department of Tourism, Royal Government of Bhutan

history.change: Fee policy revised; Wikipedia records the Indian visitor rate as unchanged since then.
Fee for other nationalities cut from 200 to 100 United States dollars a night; Indian rate not changed.

rules.title: Bhutan: 4,500 ngultrum a day for your vehicle
rules.detail: Charged per vehicle per day, two-wheelers included, and paid at the port of entry after documents and vehicle are inspected.
rules.set_by: Department of Tourism, Royal Government of Bhutan

source.title: Guidelines For Indians visiting Bhutan as Tourists

rules.title: Bhutan: papers for an Indian-registered motorcycle
rules.detail: Original driving licence and registration certificate, insurance, and emission and roadworthiness certificate. The vehicle must be under ten years old and ridden by its owner, or carry an authority letter.
rules.set_by: Royal Government of Bhutan, as stated by the Embassy of India, Thimphu

source.title: Guidelines For Indians visiting Bhutan as Tourists

rules.title: Bhutan: register the vehicle for police check posts
rules.detail: Visitors with their own vehicle register on the Royal Bhutan Police check post system before crossing check points.

source.title: Guidelines For Indians visiting Bhutan as Tourists

rules.title: Bhutan: a guide must accompany self-riders
rules.detail: The tourism department says a guide must accompany visitors at all times, and those driving their own vehicle pay for the guide on top of the vehicle fee.
rules.set_by: Department of Tourism, Royal Government of Bhutan

rules.title: Bhutan: stay only in certified accommodation
rules.detail: The Indian embassy's guidelines say visitors planning their own trip must stay in accommodation certified by the tourism department for the whole trip.
rules.set_by: Department of Tourism, Royal Government of Bhutan

source.title: Guidelines For Indians visiting Bhutan as Tourists

rules.title: Bhutan: route permit beyond Thimphu and Paro unclear
rules.detail: The tourism department says no route permit is needed with a guide. The Indian embassy page still says one is needed beyond Thimphu and Paro, issued in Thimphu on weekdays.
rules.set_by: Department of Immigration, Royal Government of Bhutan

rules.title: Bhutan: travel insurance, required or advised
rules.detail: The Indian embassy lists travel insurance among the entry permit papers and says it can be bought at the border. The tourism department calls it strongly recommended, not mandatory.
rules.set_by: Department of Tourism, Royal Government of Bhutan

source.title: Guidelines For Indians visiting Bhutan as Tourists

rules.title: Bhutan: limits on Indian currency notes
rules.detail: The embassy page allows notes up to 500 rupees, to a total of 25,000 rupees; anything above that must be in notes of 100 rupees or less.
rules.set_by: Royal Government of Bhutan, as stated by the Embassy of India, Thimphu

source.title: Embassy of India, Thimphu: information for Indian nationals entering Bhutan

season.note: No road on this route has an announced seasonal closure; landslides in the monsoon and snow in winter can block it.

hazards.title: Landslides in the monsoon, snow and frost in winter
hazards.detail: Wikipedia notes unstable geology with frequent slips, made worse by summer rain and by winter snowstorms and frost.

hazards.title: Long wait for permits at the border
hazards.detail: The tourism department warns that applying at the point of entry can mean a long wait, depending on how many applicants there are.

gaps: The tourism department and the Indian embassy disagree on whether a route permit is needed for Punakha; not resolved.
The two sources also differ on travel insurance and on the age band for the half-rate fee (6 to 11 against 6 to 12).
The Indian embassy's guidelines carry no date; the file name suggests 29 November of an unknown year.
No Bhutanese transport authority page was found naming the office that inspects vehicles and collects the daily fee at Phuentsholing.
Whether the daily vehicle fee is waived inside Phuentsholing town was not found.
Office hours and closed days of the Phuentsholing immigration office not found.
The immigration portal returned only its title and was not read.
No dated news source found for landslides or fog on the Phuentsholing to Thimphu road.
Usual number of days not sourced; highway numbers not sourced.
Wikipedia names a higher pass at Chapcha on the main road without giving its altitude; Dochula is recorded as the highest sourced point.
Web search budget ran out before this route; all facts come from pages opened directly.
Some stretch distances are doubtful. The open map may not know the road riders use, so the routing service went the long way round.
